neighborhoods.name: SoMa / Mid-Market (995 Market–5th–9th St corridor)
neighborhoods.rationale: Densest cluster of real 2025-26 dev/AI events: Frontier Tower (995 Market) hosts 3+ hackathons/day incl. Dendritic AI Hackathon (Oct 23 2025), Artificial Labor Hackathon, Prediction Market Hackathon; House of AI (40 Boardman Pl) is purpose-built for 80–200-person Tech Week hackathons; AWS GenAI Loft (525 Market) runs monthly AICamp GenAI hackathons; a16z speedrun Demo Day, GPU MODE IRL, and most Open Source AI Week parties (88 Colin P Kelly Jr St, 210 King St, 329 Bryant) all landed here. Bilingual-friendly (AWS Loft and Frontier Tower regularly host JP/KR delegations; PyLadies SF, Cloudflare MCP Night, Gemma Dev Meetup ran in the same blocks). Best transit (BART/Muni/Caltrain).
avoid_too: South of Market warehouses framed as 'event lofts' with no AV/wifi — many are Airbnb-style photo studios, not event-capable
Moscone Center itself (Dreamforce crowd, corporate, booking lead time 12+ months, dwarfs a 50–200 person coffee day)
The Midway (900 Marin) — Dogpatch, 40,000 sq ft, built for 1,500+ corporate summits; overkill and far from the hack crowd
Chronicle Books 680 2nd St — hosted GDG/Afore hackathon Oct 2025 but books out months ahead and is a publisher office, not a public cafe

neighborhoods.name: Hayes Valley (Cerebral Valley / The Commons SV)
neighborhoods.rationale: The actual 'Cerebral Valley' — The Commons SF (540 Laguna) is the named hub in Mission Local's AI venue map hosting AI hackathons, LLM study nights and philosophy-of-AI speaker series; Supabase/Apollo/Postman/Claude community meetups and SAP's Tech Week 'Adapt or Be Automated' all ran Hayes Valley listings during SF Tech Week Oct 2025; Anchor/Founders Inc and the AGI House / hacker-house network radiate out from here; walkable to cafes (Ritual, Blue Bottle Linden) that already absorb 50–200-person overflow for builder events. Strong bilingual crossover because J-pop adjacent Patricia Mou / The Commons programming explicitly courts JP/Intl founders.
avoid_too: Strictly members-only clubs (Shack15-style pricing) — Hayes has small boutiques; verify walk-in event hire before committing
Residential side streets off Laguna — 'hacker house' events are invite-only and not bilingual-friendly
The Heron Arts / Fort Mason pop-ups — sometimes tagged Hayes Valley but actually Marina, far and tiny
Anything above 250 pax — venues here cap out around 150; don't oversell size

neighborhoods.name: The Mission (16th–20th, Mission–Valencia corridor)
neighborhoods.rationale: Real hack history: AICamp's monthly 'AI MCP Agent Hackathon' runs at Wefunder / 1885 Mission St (recurring through 2025); Noisebridge (2169 Mission) hosts a 400+ member AI group with weekly paper-reading and AI-lit nights; SF Tech Week 2025 listed Mission events incl. Tech Bio Founders Breakfast and the Mission Dolores Manor 'Hotpot + Founders' Pitch' (Oct 11); anchor coffee/event space Stable Café (2128 Folsom) and Borderlands Cafe already absorb 50–200 pax creative/bilingual events. Most bilingual-friendly of the three (long JP/LatAm community presence, Japan Town–adjacent bus lines, Code for San Francisco civic bilingual hack nights).
avoid_too: Mission Dolores Manor and similar private mansions — invite-only, sparse walkable cafe backup
Noisebridge itself as the primary venue — anarchist maker space, no event hire, no booking desk
Tartine Manufactory / Heath complex on 18th — books out for private events 6+ months ahead, ~80 pax max
Valencia St bar-cafes — most cap at 40–60 pax and are evening-noise-licensed, bad for a 9am–6pm coffee/hack day
